column1: # Pass 2 rulebook source (hand-authored). Columns: id | scope | severity | anchors | paraphrase (ours)
# anchors: ';'-separated (split only before '<digits>:') "<section ordinal>:<verbatim snippet>" (each snippet ≤ 25 words, must occur in exactly that section;
#   resolved to passage ids by book-rules.py). The first anchor's snippet becomes the optional quote.
# scope: all | pranayama | mudras | asanas | meditation | conduct | <candidate ids from map.json, comma-separated>
# severity: hard-stop (engine/player must enforce or block) | caution (shown as a warning / caps progression) |
#   guidance (default behaviour or copy) | info (Ask material) | traditional (recorded, not enforced or ported)

guru-for-advanced|all|caution|32:You can get easy lessons from the Guru and practise them at home also in the initial stages of practice;32:for advanced and difficult exercises you will have to stay with the Guru;137:The actual method of awakening the Kundalini Shakti and uniting Her with the Lord in the Sahasrara can only be learnt from a Guru|Easy lessons can be learnt and practised at home; advanced Kundalini work (moving prana into the central channel, piercing the knots) needs a personal teacher.

advanced-mudras-guru-only|mudras,khechari,vajroli,shakti-chalana|hard-stop|109:Khechari, Shakti Chalana, Vajroli and other advanced courses should not be practised by all;104:only if he has undergone the preliminary exercise under the direct guidance of a Guru;105:This must be done under the direct guidance of a Guru|Khechari, shakti chalana, vajroli and the other advanced kriyas are only for those a teacher has judged fit; never runnable alone.

khechari-guru-and-age|khechari|hard-stop|109:Khechari Mudra should be done under the direct guidance of a Khechari Guru;109:Aspirants may not be successful in this Kriya if they begin after 25 years of age;175:It has to be learnt under a developed Yogi Guru who has practised this Yoga for a long time|Khechari (tongue lengthening) only under a teacher who practises it; the book adds it seldom succeeds if begun after 25.

purity-before-awakening|all|caution|60:People must have purity first; then a thorough knowledge of the Sadhana, a proper guide, and a steady, gradual practice;60:awakens the Sakti by sheer force through Asanas, Pranayamas and Mudras, he will break his legs|Ethical and mental preparation comes before any attempt to awaken Kundalini; forcing it with techniques is said to cause harm.

no-premature-awakening|all|caution|136:Premature awakening is not desirable;136:Do not bother much about awakening Kundalini|Do not chase awakening; purify and steady the mind and let it come in its own time. Practices must never promise awakening.

gradual-no-violence|all|caution|187:No sudden and violent methods should be employed;187:The practice of Yoga should be gradual and step by step|Practise gradually and step by step; avoid extremes and violent methods.

master-lower-steps|all|guidance|136:Do not take up any higher courses before you completely master the lower steps;136:There is no use of jumping into Dhyana without having the various preliminary practices|Master each stage (ethics, posture, breath) before moving to the next.

one-method|all|guidance|80:There will be no use if you jump from one exercise to another every day;187:choose a method and stick to it and persevere in it continuously;94:Never change the Asanas|Choose one method or set and keep to it; hopping between exercises daily gives no benefit.

empty-stomach|all|guidance|94:Asana should be done on empty stomach in the morning or at least three hours after food;109:Mudras and Bandhas also should be practised when the stomach is empty;30:you should not practise when the stomach is loaded|Practise on an empty stomach: early morning, or about three hours after a meal.

early-morning|all|guidance|30:Early morning hours are suitable for Yogic practices;80:Early morning, answer the calls of nature and sit for the Yogic practices;179:Practise Asanas and Pranayama in the early morning or three hours after food|Early morning (after the toilet) is the best time; cool hours in general; in hot places avoid practising in the heat of the day.

bath-before-not-after|all|guidance|30:Generally Yogic practices should be done only after a bath;80:Do not take bath immediately after Pranayama is over. Take rest for half an hour|Bathe before practice, not straight after; after pranayama rest about half an hour first.
not-when-agitated|all|guidance|30:You should not sit for Yogic practices when your mind is restless or when you are worried much|Do not start a session while very restless or worried.

quiet-clean-place|all|guidance|29:Sadhana should be done in a secluded place. There should be no interruption by anyone;80:Practise Pranayama in a dry, welt-ventilated room|A quiet, clean, dry, well-ventilated place free of interruption; keep to one place.

seat-height|all|guidance|29:Your Asana (seat) for the Yogic practices should not be too high or too low;147:take a pure and pleasant seat which is neither too high nor too low|Sit on a firm mat or folded blanket, neither too high nor too low.

age|all|caution|31:Young boys under 18 years of age whose bodies are very tender should not have too much practice;31:the best period for Yoga Abhyasa is from 20 to 40 years of age;136:young age is not suitable for advanced courses in Yoga|Under-18s should practise only lightly and never the advanced courses; healthy people can begin even after 50.

moderate-diet|conduct|guidance|28:Take half stomachful of wholesome food. Fill a quarter with pure water. Leave the rest free;142:He should fill half the stomach with food|Moderate eating: half the stomach food, a quarter water, a quarter empty; change diet gradually.
no-heavy-fasting|conduct|caution|28:Do not fast much. It will produce weakness in you|Avoid frequent fasting; it weakens. Break a fast with something light.

sattvic-diet|conduct|traditional|27:Sour, hot, pungent and bitter preparations, salt, mustard, asafoetida, chillies;26:I will give you a list of Sattvic articles for a Sadhaka|Recommended light vegetarian foods and a list of foods to avoid (stimulating, sour, meat, eggs, onion, garlic, alcohol). Recorded, not enforced.

renunciate-conduct|conduct|traditional|136:Brahmacharya is very very essential;24:Mixing with householders is highly dangerous for a Sadhaka;136:Avoid the company of women|Celibacy, silence, solitude and avoiding company (including women and householders) are framed for male renunciates. Recorded for completeness; not ported to app copy.

body-care|all|guidance|136:All possible care should be taken to keep the body in a healthy condition;94:The instrument must be kept clean, strong and healthy|Look after the body's health; austerity is not an excuse to neglect it.

gloom-means-error|all|caution|136:If a practitioner is gloomy, depressed and weak, surely there is some error in his Sadhana;80:There must be always joy and exhilaration of spirit during and after the practice|Practice should leave you refreshed and cheerful; persistent gloom, weakness or fatigue means the practice is wrong and should be eased.

jerks-early|all|info|136:In the beginning of your practice, you may get jerks of hands, legs, trunk and whole body|Involuntary jerks may occur early on; the book calls them harmless and passing. Ask material only; never scripted.

backache-not-kundalini|all|info|136:Do not take the movements of rheumatic winds in the back from chronic lumbago for ascent of Kundalini|Back pains and sensations are not Kundalini rising; do not read bodily symptoms as attainment.

reject-siddhis|all|guidance|136:The Yogi who is bent upon getting the highest Samadhi, must reject Siddhis whenever they come;117:he stops there by the influence of Maya and false Tushti|Powers are distractions to be ignored; never offer them as goals or narrate them.

signs-not-targets|all|info|10:These indicate that the Kundalini Shakti has been awakened;133:Various kinds of lights manifest during meditation owing to deep concentration|Visions, lights and sounds are described as signs; they are Ask material with the book's handling, never a target or a scripted line.

mantra-from-guru|meditation,nadi-suddhi-bija|caution|113:Aspirants in Kundalini Yoga should take to this Mantra Sadhana only after getting a proper Mantra from a Guru|Kundalini mantra practice should use a mantra received from a teacher; bija sequences stay teacher-only.
spiritual-diary|all|guidance|139:Maintain a daily diary and realise the marvellous results|Keep a daily practice log (sleep, japa, pranayama, asana, meditation, silence, service).

kumbhaka-no-face-strain|pranayama|hard-stop|80:Some people twist the muscles of the face when they do Kumbhaka;80:It is also a symptom to indicate that they are going beyond their capacity|Straining the face during a hold means you are past your capacity: shorten the hold.

no-suffocation|pranayama|hard-stop|80:you should not experience the feeling of suffocation or discomfort at any stage of Pranayama;80:You should never feel the necessity of catching hold of a few normal breaths between any two successive rounds|Set inhale, hold and exhale so there is never suffocation and no need for recovery breaths between rounds; a gasp means the hold was too long.
no-fatigue|pranayama|caution|80:Do not perform the Pranayama till you are fatigued|Stop before tiredness; finish refreshed.

beginners-no-kumbhaka|pranayama|hard-stop|80:A neophyte should do Puraka and Rechaka only without any Kumbhaka for some days;80:The proportion for Puraka and Rechaka is 1:2|Beginners breathe in and out only (exhale twice the inhale, 1:2) for some days before any hold. This is the beginner form of every retention practice.

kumbhaka-weekly-build|pranayama|caution|80:Retain for 4 seconds in the first week, for 8 seconds in the second week and for 12 seconds in the third week|Build the hold slowly: about 4 s in week one, 8 s in week two, 12 s in week three, then gradually. The engine's 30 s cap still applies.

comfortable-hold|pranayama|caution|71:Be careful in doing the Kumbhaka as long as you can comfortably do;72:The period of Kumbhaka also should be gradually and cautiously increased|Hold only as long as is comfortable and increase it cautiously.

smooth-exhale-after-hold|pranayama|caution|80:you must have efficient control over the lungs at the end of Kumbhaka|Only hold as long as you can still exhale smoothly and in proportion afterwards; do not over-lengthen the exhale either.

slow-silent-breath|pranayama|guidance|80:Always inhale and exhale very slowly. Do not make any sound;80:In Pranayamas like Bhastrika and Kapalabhati, you can produce a mild or the lowest possible sound|Breathe slowly and quietly; bhastrika and kapalabhati may make a soft sound (ujjayi's throat sound is the book's own exception).

ratio-1-4-2|sukha-purvaka,kundalini-pranayama-muladhara,nadi-suddhi-bija|guidance|71:The ratio of inhalation, retention and exhalation is 1:4:2|Inhale : hold : exhale in the ratio 1:4:2 (e.g. 3:12:6 Oms) for the retention forms.

count-then-let-go|pranayama|guidance|80:In the beginning you must observe some time-unit for Puraka, Kumbhaka and Rechaka;80:In the advanced stages, you need not distract the mind in counting|Count with Om, a mantra or numbers at first; drop counting once the ratio is natural.
steady-body|pranayama,meditation|guidance|80:The Asana should be steady and as firm as a rock when you do Pranayama, Japa and meditation|Keep the body still during breath practice and meditation.
clean-nostrils|pranayama|guidance|80:Before you sit for Pranayama practice, thoroughly clean the nostrils|Clear the nostrils before practice.

fifteen-minutes-daily|pranayama|guidance|80:At least you must have 15 minutes’ daily practice in the beginning regularly for days together|Beginners: at least 15 minutes a day, regularly; results are not instant.

after-practice|pranayama|traditional|80:take a cup of milk or light tiffin after 10 minutes;80:If you get perspiration during the practice, do not wipe it with a towel. Rub it with your hand|Light food about 10 minutes after; rub sweat in by hand; avoid cold draughts.

bhastrika-build|bhastrika|caution|72:Begin with 10 expulsions for a round and increase it gradually to 20 or 25 for a round;72:Do 3 rounds in the beginning|Bhastrika starts at 10 breaths a round and 3 rounds with rest between; build slowly.

kapalabhati-build|kapalabhati|guidance|66:To start with, have only one expulsion per second. In the beginning do 10 expulsions per round|Kapalabhati: about one forced exhale per second, 10 per round at first, adding 10 at a time up to 120.
sukha-purvaka-build|sukha-purvaka|guidance|71:To start with do 6 Pranayamas in the morning and 6 in the evening|Sukha Purvaka: 6 rounds morning and evening to start, rising to 20.

suryabheda-hold-limit|suryabheda|caution|73:Hold the breath till perspiration oozes from the roots of the hair;73:This point cannot be reached at the very outset|The book's limit for the suryabheda hold is sweating at the hair roots, reached only over time. We treat this as a teacher-only form; the engine caps holds at 30 s.

trataka-sun-guide|trataka|hard-stop|65:The last one, sun-gazing should not be attempted until you get the help of an experienced man|Never sun-gaze without an experienced guide; the engine never offers sun trataka.

trataka-eyes|trataka|caution|65:Do not tax your eyes by over-practice;65:Those who have very weak eye-capillaries should do Trataka after closing their eyes on any imaginary spot|Do not strain the eyes; with weak eyes gaze at an imagined point with eyes closed; close the eyes when tired.
trataka-start|trataka|guidance|65:Do Trataka for two minutes to start with. Then cautiously increase the period|Start trataka at about two minutes and lengthen cautiously.
plavini-expert|plavini|hard-stop|75:The help of one who is well versed in this Pranayama, is necessary|Plavini (air-swallowing) only with an expert's help.

bandha-phases|mula-bandha,jalandhara-bandha,uddiyana-bandha,bandha-traya|guidance|109:Mula Bandha is practised during Puraka, Kumbhaka, Rechaka and during meditation and Japa also;109:Uddiyana Bandha is practised during Rechaka and Jalandhara Bandha during Kumbhaka|Root lock may be held in any breath phase and in meditation; chin lock belongs to the held breath; abdominal lock to the end of the hold / start of the exhale.
uddiyana-empty-lungs|uddiyana-bandha|caution|98:Empty the lungs by a strong and forcible expiration|Uddiyana is done on emptied lungs: an exhaled hold, so the retention rules apply.
mudras-combine|mudras|info|109:The benefits that are given may not be realised by the practice of Mudras alone|Mudras work together with breath, posture and japa, and need concentration.
yoni-mudra-caution|yoni-mudra|caution|107:Therefore realise the importance of this Mudra and practise it very cautiously|Yoni mudra is called difficult; practise it cautiously.
viparitakarani-build|viparitakarani|caution|103:On the first day do it for a minute|Viparitakarani starts at one minute and grows slowly.

asana-basics|asanas|guidance|94:Spread a blanket on the floor and practise the Asanas over the blanket;94:Do not wear spectacles when you do Asanas|Practise asanas on a blanket, without spectacles, regularly, as one fixed set.

headstand-build|asanas|caution|86:Stand for five seconds in the beginning and gradually increase the period by 15 seconds each week|Headstand builds from about 5 s by 15 s a week, entering and leaving slowly.
urdhva-padmasana-prereq|asanas|hard-stop|93:If you can stand in Sirshasana for more than 10 or 15 minutes, then you can attempt this|Lotus-in-headstand only after a steady 10–15 minute headstand.

upanishad-kumbhaka-schedule|pranayama|caution|151:On the first day, Kumbhaka should be practised four times;151:with an increase of five times each day|The Upanishad's schedule (4, then 10 + 5, then 20, adding 5 a day with all three locks) is far steeper than the book's own gradual rules; treat as teacher-only.

obstacles|all|info|152:Seven are the causes of the diseases in the body;136:If a Yogi is affected by any disease due to these causes, he says that the disease is due to his Yogic practice|The listed causes of illness and obstacles to practice (day sleep, late nights, crowds, bad food, suppressing urges, doubt, laziness…).
